benchmark_study.citation: Ogulur et al. (2023). Gut epithelial barrier damage caused by dishwasher detergents and rinse aids. Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology (JACI), 151(2), 469-484.

washers.name: Commercial Conveyor / Flight Dishwasher (Cafeteria / Hospital)
washers.description: High-speed conveyor washer. Dishes receive chemical rinse aid injector at 85°C followed by forced air flash dry with zero freshwater rinse. Leaves the highest chemical residue.

washers.name: Commercial Pass-Through Hood Dishwasher (Restaurant / Catering)
washers.description: Standard restaurant machine. High-concentration surfactant injected into final hot rinse; plates air-dry in racks with zero secondary clean water rinse.

washers.name: Commercial Bar Glasswasher (Café / Bar / Pub)
washers.description: Ultra-fast bar cycle designed to eliminate water spotting on glassware. High alcohol ethoxylate dose creates rapid sheen but deposits persistent dry surfactant film.

washers.name: Domestic Residential Dishwasher (Pots & Pans Intensive Cycle)
washers.description: Extended residential wash (140 min) with 3 dedicated clean water intermediate rinses and prolonged drain stages, substantially diluting rinse aid chemicals.

washers.name: Domestic Residential Dishwasher (Eco / Quick 50°C Cycle)
washers.description: Water-saving cycle with fewer rinse liters and lower wash temperature, slightly reducing detergent and surfactant wash-off efficacy.

washers.name: Manual Handwashing with Freshwater Running Tap Rinse
washers.description: Plates scrubbed with natural or mild detergent and thoroughly flushed under continuous running potable tap water. Near-zero surfactant carryover.

substrates.name: Melamine / Polypropylene / Polycarbonate (Commercial Trays & Bowls)
substrates.notes: Hydrophobic polymer surface with microscopic surface abrasions tenaciously binds amphiphilic non-ionic alcohol ethoxylates.

substrates.name: Food-Grade Silicone (Infant Plates, Suction Bowls, Spoons)
substrates.notes: Organosilicon matrix readily absorbs surfactant molecules into its porous polymer lattice, slowly leaching into food.

substrates.name: Vitrified Glazed Ceramic / Porcelain (Standard Dinner Plates)
substrates.notes: Smooth non-porous vitreous glaze acts as the neutral baseline reference for chemical residue retention.

substrates.name: Soda-Lime / Borosilicate Glass (Cups, Wine Glasses, Mugs)
substrates.notes: Surfactant forms an optical thin film that dries clear; instantly solubilized upon contact with hot or acidic liquids.

substrates.name: 18/10 Stainless Steel (Cutlery, Food Service Pans, Bowls)
substrates.notes: Passive chromium oxide passivation layer has minimal electrostatic and chemical affinity for non-ionic surfactants.

food_matrices.name: Hot Acidic Beverage (Coffee, Tea, Tomato Soup, Citrus Broth)
food_matrices.notes: High temperature and low pH rapidly strip almost the entirety of dried surfactant residues directly into the beverage.

food_matrices.name: Fatty / Lipophilic Meal (Cream Soup, Curry, Oily Pasta, Stew)
food_matrices.notes: Dietary lipids solubilize amphiphilic alcohol ethoxylates instantaneously, ensuring high intestinal absorption.

food_matrices.name: Warm Moderate Food (Rice, Steamed Vegetables, Grilled Chicken)
food_matrices.notes: Partial surface contact transfer without full dissolution of surfactant molecules.

food_matrices.name: Cold Water / Chilled Soft Drink / Milk
food_matrices.notes: Moderate dissolution into cold aqueous liquid during prolonged drinking or soaking.

food_matrices.name: Dry Finger Food (Bread, Crackers, Dry Sandwich, Fruit)
food_matrices.notes: Minimal contact transfer with low solvent extraction into dry carbohydrates.

clinical_profiles.name: General Healthy Adult (Intact Mucosal Barrier)
clinical_profiles.description: Normal intestinal goblet cell density, continuous MUC2 mucin synthesis, and robust physiological epithelial regeneration.

clinical_profiles.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Crohn's Disease / Ulcerative Colitis)
clinical_profiles.description: Pre-existing mucosal barrier defects and depleted tight junctions. Alcohol ethoxylate exposure triggers rapid alarmin release and mucosal inflammation flares.

clinical_profiles.name: Celiac Disease / Severe Food Allergy / Eosinophilic Esophagitis
clinical_profiles.description: Compromised paracellular seals allow undigested food peptides (e.g. gliadin fragments) to cross into the lamina propria, amplifying immune sensitization.

clinical_profiles.name: Infant or Toddler (< 3 Years Old, Immature Gut Barrier)
clinical_profiles.description: Developmentally immature tight junction complexes and thin mucus layer. Extremely vulnerable to synthetic surfactant cytotoxicity on silicone plates.

clinical_profiles.name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) / SIBO / Gut Dysbiosis
clinical_profiles.description: Subclinical low-grade mucosal inflammation and visceral hypersensitivity exacerbated by surfactant-induced epithelial barrier leaks.
